research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register text (27 FR 6653) prints Executive Order 11036 as an order of the President (John F. Kennedy) dated 1962-07-11; the number, subject and date agree with the census register row (subject: Administration of the Agricultural Trade Development and Assistance Act of 1954, as amended). I read the whole text and signature block. Inventory: the dossier splits the order into two contiguous clauses at an OCR break inside amended Section 4(a)(1) (the second clause begins with a sentence fragment labelled Section 104). Together they cover amendments (I), (II) and (III) and the signature; I confirm the inventory as complete and decide both clauses as parts of one amending order. The order further amends Executive Order No. 10900 of January 5, 1961, as amended (administration of the Agricultural Trade Development and Assistance Act of 1954): (I) it substitutes a new Section 4(a), under which the Director of the Bureau of the Budget fixes the amounts of foreign currencies accruing under Title I to be used for section 104 purposes and notifies the Secretary of the Treasury, and the waiver function of the penultimate proviso of section 104 is delegated to the Secretary of State for section 104(e) and to the Director of the Bureau of the Budget otherwise; (II) it inserts a new paragraph (5) in Section 4(d) assigning section 104(s) purposes to the Department of the Treasury in consultation with the Department of State and delegating the terms-and-conditions function to the Secretary of the Treasury; and (III) it substitutes a new Section 4(d)(7) assigning section 104(g) purposes to the Department of State and delegating the loan-manner function to the Secretary of State. Ending: Executive Order 12220 of June 27, 1980 (45 FR 44245, Federal Register of July 1, 1980; the complete held Federal Register text) provides in section 1-501 that Executive Order No. 10900 of January 5, 1961, as amended, is revoked. Because this order's text is part of Executive Order 10900 as amended, that revocation reaches it, and the same order re-delegates each function in revised form: section 1-401(a) addresses the use of foreign currencies, the fixing of amounts by the Director of the Office of Management and Budget and the notice to the Treasury, section 1-401(b) re-delegates the waiver function (to the Director of the United States International Development Cooperation Agency for section 104(e) and to the Director of the Office of Management and Budget otherwise), section 1-405(a) re-delegates the loan-manner function formerly in Section 4(d)(7), and section 1-405(b) re-delegates the terms-and-conditions function formerly in Section 4(d)(5) to the Secretary of the Treasury in consultation with the Secretary of State. The held text has no effective-date wording and is headed as an order of June 27, 1980, so I read 1980-06-27 as the effective date; the alternative reading is the publication date, 1980-07-01. The dossier's located-provision record for this pair uses a transcription mirror of EO 12220; I did not rely on it and cite the Federal Register text instead. Savings: the functions continue under Executive Order 12220, which re-delegates them in revised form; EO 12220 has no express savings clause in the held text (reviewed in full). Searches selected after reading their coverage notes (all three complete, no coverage warning): U.S. Code release point 119-121 (no hit for this order), eCFR as of 2026-10-14 (no hit), and the Federal Register catalog disposition notes (2 machine hits, the revocation note on this order and the matching note on EO 12553).

savings.reason: The delegations amended or added by this order were re-delegated in revised form in sections 1-401(a)-(b) and 1-405(a)-(b) of Executive Order 12220, which revoked Executive Order 10900 as amended on 1980-06-27; the functions therefore continued, with revised delegates in places, under the new order. The held text of Executive Order 12220 has no express savings clause, and no U.S. Code, eCFR or Federal Register catalog hit shows any other continuing effect of this order.
